summary: Ground explicit Email participant display names to one complete same-role header value in their own citations.
decision_refs: The active objective requires accurate file-grounded questions across RFI, Submittal and Email content
An offline reproduction proved that a cited Email recipient name could be presented as the sender when the answer omitted addresses
A bounded same-role header-value check closes the structured participant gap using Python's standard library without another model request
approval_evidence: The persistent objective authorizes bounded accuracy and adaptability improvements to the existing file-grounded question flow.
known_limitations: Only explicit sender, recipient, From, To, Cc, Bcc and Reply-To display-name claims enter this guard; it does not infer a participant from ordinary prose.
Only evidence conservatively classified as Email can ground an Email participant; an RFI or Submittal form's From or To field remains its own source type.
Case, repeated whitespace and outer quotation marks normalize while the complete participant value and role stay exact.
The guard does not infer identity from an address, company, title or signature, decode encoded headers, unfold new source formats, choose the current thread message or determine authority.
Header unfolding and encoded-word decoding remain responsibilities of the existing Email parser; this change does not connect to a mailbox or alter source parsing.
